title: Tokenflow smoothing controller and guarded prefetch rollback for multi-tenant latency surge
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: A subset of multi-tenant workloads observed a regression in first-token latency (TTFT) and a sustained drop in tokens/sec after the kernel-scheduling heuristics and an aggressive KV-prefetch change were deployed to hosted and dedicated pools. The degradation was most visible for heterogeneous context-window sessions and for Private/VPC deployments using multiplexed workers. A customer (internal escalation from "Acme Labs" support) reported a 2–3x TTFT increase on chat endpoints for long-history sessions. This ticket coordinates fast rollback mitigations, a short-term smoothing controller, and a long-term guarded prefetch strategy to prevent recurrence across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Median TTFT for affected workloads returns to within 10% of baseline across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; 2) Tokens/sec for representative multiplexed model traffic recovers to baseline within 24h of mitigation; 3) Canary rollout with guarded prefetch enabled shows no regression on synthetic heterogeneous context tests; 4) Automated regression test added to runtime CI that simulates mixed-context multiplexing and validates TTFT and tokens/sec thresholds.
investigation_notes: Investigation timeline: 2026-03-08 08:30 - alert spike detected on latency-page (Customer HL). 2026-03-08 09:10 - oncall paged runtime and serving teams. 2026-03-08 10:00 - reproduced locally using a synthetic harness that replays multiplexed sessions with mixed context lengths; saw KV-prefetch filling the worker memory and provoking kernel preemption behavior leading to head-of-line stalls. 2026-03-08 12:30 - confirmed correlation with recent kernel scheduling tweak (kernel-selector v2.9.1) and kv-prefetch aggressive window introduced in runtime-1.24 rollout. 2026-03-09 15:00 - load-tested rollback of kv-prefetch and observed immediate TTFT recovery on canary. Key hypothesis: aggressive prefetch increases KV cache churn for long-session keys across multiplexed connections, causing kernel selector to reassign work and evict warming kernels, creating repeated cold starts for initial tokens.
mitigation_runbook: 1) Immediately toggle runtime flag runtime.prefetch.enabled=false in affected clusters (Hosted regional pool us-west-2-dedicated and Private clusters with multiplexing enabled). 2) Deploy tokenflow-smoothing controller (rate limiter per-session + small initial token cap) to cap inflight initial-token work and reduce head-of-line pressure (canary patch deployed 2026-03-09 18:00). 3) Roll back kernel-selector v2.9.1 to v2.9.0 in the most impacted dedicated pools where rollback is safe. 4) If rollback not feasible for Private customers, apply per-tenant guarded prefetch profile: prefetch disabled for multiplex sessions with >2 context windows and enabled for single-tenant long-batches. 5) Monitor dashboards: org/latency/ttft and org/throughput/tokens-sec with alerts for median TTFT > 1.2x baseline or tokens/sec drop > 25%.
decisions: - Short-term decision: disable aggressive kv-prefetch cluster-wide for multiplexed workers and enable tokenflow-smoothing controller (agreed at 2026-03-09 17:30 incident call). - Long-term decision: replace aggressive prefetch with a guarded prefetch policy that uses a per-session score (history depth, multiplex factor, model variant) before issuing prefetch. - Add regression test coverage and a new telemetry dimension 'prefetch_score' to make root-cause analysis easier.
next_steps: 1) Finish PR for smoothing controller (PR ready for review: see links). 2) Land canary rollback for kernel-selector in hosted pools and monitor for 6 hours. 3) Draft guarded prefetch design doc and run through architecture review with Applied ML and Runtime teams (target design review 2026-03-12). 4) Add CI synthetic test and schedule nightly runs against runtime-stable branch.
